title: The Analytics GraphQL API exposes a single analytics.series(filter) query and accepts no writes at all
content:
The entire GraphQL surface of the Analytics Engine is one field:

```graphql
type AnalyticsQuery {
  series(filter: AnalyticsFilter): [AnalyticsPeriod]
}

extend type Query {
  analytics: AnalyticsQuery
}
```

No mutations are declared anywhere in the schema, and the docs state it plainly: data cannot be input through GraphQL. Writes go through `IAnalyticsStore` in TypeScript, from a processor or a script. Treat the GraphQL layer as strictly a reporting surface.

`AnalyticsFilter` must be **fully populated** — it is not a partial where the engine fills in defaults. All six of `start`, `end`, `granularity`, `metrics`, `dimensions` (each with `name`, `select`, `lod`), and `currency` are required for the query to function. The characteristic symptom of a partial filter is not a validation message but a bare `"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'filter')"`.

Case sensitivity is the other common failure. Metric names and granularity values are matched exactly, so `Monthlyu` produces an enum error suggesting `monthly`, and a mistyped metric produces an error listing the valid names.

A useful exploration technique from the best-practices page: start with a broad `select` and a high `lod` (e.g. `select: "atlas"`, `lod: 5`) to *discover* which sub-paths exist under a dimension, then narrow the `select` path once you know the hierarchy. The high-lod response is effectively a directory listing of the dimension tree.

description: AnalyticsQuery has exactly one field, series(filter: AnalyticsFilter), reached via extend type Query { analytics }. There is no Mutation, and a partial filter errors out.
